code.originalText: Twelve-week review: blood pressure and lipids after a gout flare on hydrochlorothiazide; switch to losartan

text.paragraph: Twelve-week review of blood pressure and lipids three weeks after a gout flare on hydrochlorothiazide. [S]

Mr. Cook returns three weeks after the same-day visit for gout of his right big toe. The pain settled within four days of colchicine, he took the last tablet five days after starting, and he had no diarrhea or muscle aches. He has had no further attacks. He continues hydrochlorothiazide, amlodipine, atorvastatin and aspirin without missed doses. His home readings average 132/80. He has had no stroke symptoms. His Social Security retirement benefits and Medicare have been approved, and he has signed a six-month lease on his room. He is writing most mornings and says he feels steadier. [S]

list.item:
Drug-induced gout, first flare, resolved (M10.271). Serum urate 8.4 mg/dL three weeks after the flare, on hydrochlorothiazide. The 2020 ACR guideline advises switching hydrochlorothiazide to another blood pressure drug when feasible, and losartan, which lowers urate, is a good choice. After a single flare, without kidney disease, tophi, kidney stones or a urate above 9 mg/dL, urate-lowering drugs are not started. [S]
Stop hydrochlorothiazide.
No urate-lowering drug now; reconsider if flares recur.
Fewer sugary drinks and less red meat and shellfish; no alcohol.

Essential hypertension, not yet at target (I10). Office 134/80 and home 132/80, still above 130/80. Sodium 137, potassium 3.7 mmol/L, creatinine 1.04 mg/dL, eGFR 80, the baseline before a renin-angiotensin drug. [S]
Losartan 50 mg daily in place of hydrochlorothiazide; continue amlodipine 5 mg.
Potassium and creatinine one to two weeks after starting losartan.
Review in four weeks.

Asymptomatic right internal carotid stenosis (I65.21). LDL 68 mg/dL from 148, a 54 percent reduction, ten weeks after starting atorvastatin 40 mg; total cholesterol 142, HDL 48, triglycerides 130 mg/dL; ALT 26 U/L. No symptoms. [S]
Continue atorvastatin 40 mg and aspirin 81 mg.
Repeat lipid panel in 6 to 12 months.
Repeat duplex in about ten months.

Re-entry after incarceration (Z65.2). Housing and income are now settled; mood steadier. [S]
Second hepatitis B vaccine dose today.
Repeat PHQ-9 at the next visit.
